documents.abstract: Solar energy production forecasting is crucial for optimally integrating renewable energy sources into power systems. Deep learning techniques have emerged as promising alternatives for solar energy forecasting in recent years.In this study; Modeling, simulation and estimation of solar energy that can be produced next year of the solar power plant with a total installed power of 1300 kW, established in Bitlis province in the Eastern Anatolia Region of Turkey, are shown. PVsyst software program was used to analyze the performance ratio and different losses occurring in the system. Additionally, the study reviews deep learning techniques for solar energy forecasting with a special focus on Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks for short-term solar energy production forecasting. As a result of this examination, R2 score, MAE (Mean Absolute Error), and MSE (Mean Squared Error) were obtained as 0.863, 0.284 and 0.125, respectively. Estimated energy production in 2024 was calculated from the network trained with the LSTM model. Actual results were interpreted by comparing the results of the PVsyst program and the artificial intelligence algorithm. The study provides high-accuracy prediction to improve the integration of solar energy into power systems and reduce energy costs

Tourism is a strategic sector in India's development agenda, and scholarship on its management has expanded quickly since the pandemic. This paper reviews 52 publications from 2022 to 2026 and organizes them into five themes: (1) smart tourism, artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalization; (2) sustainability and overtourism; (3) governance, policy and law; (4) niche and special-interest tourism (adventure, medical, spiritual); and (5) economic performance and hospitality management. The review finds a marked rise in technology-oriented and Viksit Bharat 2047-linked work since 2025, alongside a persistent reliance on conceptual, descriptive and single-region designs. Three gaps stand out: little empirical validation of AI and smart-tourism frameworks, weak integration between sustainability goals and governance mechanisms, and limited attention to workforce readiness and community outcomes. A research agenda is proposed.

topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Detecting and localizing acoustic events from a person or device is important for a wide range of applications, including improving pedestrian safety, increasing situational awareness, or for interacting with digital assistants. Compared to radio frequency waves, acoustic waves are naturally more affected and attenuated by the atmosphere, making the range of sensing limited. Additionally, naturally quiet sounds like footsteps are difficult to detect. We propose SoleSense, a shoe-based platform with microphone arrays attached to the soles of both shoes, for sound event localization and detection (SELD). SoleSense takes advantage of two novel design choices to overcome attenuation and low signal strength. First, placing microphones on the shoe near the ground, compared to other human-centered platforms that are higher (e.g., headsets), provides natural near-ground acoustic amplification through pressure zone effect and access to ground-coupled cues. Second, SoleSense incorporates a novel transformer-based architecture called Soleformer that augments the standard attention-based global feature extractor (multi-head attention) with a convolutional neural network based local feature extractor, resulting in more salient features for detecting and localizing (weaker) sounds. Through realistic experiments across five different scenarios (environmental sounds, vehicles, speech, footsteps and multiple concurrent sound sources), we demonstrate that SoleSense can improve performance over current state-of-the-art SELD systems by up to 70%.

ABSTRACT Hyperspectral standoff detection systems such as Focal Plane Array (FPA) Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectrometers provide high spatial resolution in detecting airborne chemical contaminants that are invisible to the human eye but potentially hazardous. When two such systems are operated simultaneously with a suitable opening angle, they enable tomographic reconstruction of contaminant plumes with improved spatial and temporal accuracy. This work presents a mathematical model of these measurement capabilities and an algorithm to identify, localize, and quantify contaminant release sources. The objective is to develop a tool that reconstructs release locations and predicts the future plume evolution from standoff measurement data, thereby supporting early warning and situational awareness in hazardous material release scenarios. The transport of contaminants is modeled by an advection–diffusion equation, and the corresponding inverse problem for source identification is formulated accordingly. Owing to the severe ill‐posedness and underdetermination of the problem, a sparsity‐promoting regularization approach is employed together with a high‐performance optimization algorithm. To incorporate the tomographic measurement data into the discrete formulation, a level‐set description of a threshold concentration is used, allowing the measurements to be represented independently of the computational mesh and avoiding costly remeshing procedures.

topics: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

documents.abstract: Abstract Large language model agents can adjust optimization parameters in a treatment planning system under natural-language instruction, but no study has tested a model post-trained for extended reasoning against a general-purpose model in stereotactic radiosurgery. We compared a reasoning-optimized model (QwQ-32B) with a general-purpose model (Llama 3.1-70B) within SAGE, a locally hosted agent that adjusts optimization-objective priorities in Eclipse, which performs all optimization and dose calculation. Each configuration optimized 41 retrospective single-target brain metastasis cases (18 Gy, single fraction) with fixed clinical beam geometry; plans failing the clinical conformity standard (all but two) then received one standardized physicist instruction. The reasoning-optimized configuration produced a lower conformity ratio (median difference −0.20, 95% CI −0.48 to −0.10; $$q<0.001$$ ; lower in 36 of 41 cases) and lower normal-brain V12Gy ( $$q<0.001$$ ), improved conformity more after the instruction (difference in change −0.28, $$p<0.001$$ ), exceeded 21.6 Gy maximum dose less often (5 versus 12 plans), and produced fewer unparseable outputs (25 versus 122). Against clinical plans it showed no significant difference in PTV coverage, maximum dose, conformity ratio, or gradient index, and its right-cochlear maximum dose was lower, a clinically negligible difference.

The chemical industry is associated with high occupational risks due to hazardous chemicals, pressurized equipment, and complex production processes. Therefore, the implementation of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is essential to prevent workplace accidents and support sustainable industrial operations. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of OHS in the Production Plant-1 environment of PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia and identify areas requiring improvement. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed using primary and secondary data collected through direct observation, interviews, documentation studies, and analysis of the company’s I’m Safe program records. Data were processed through reduction, classification, tabulation, and presentation to assess OHS practices comprehensively. The findings show that workers consistently comply with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements and that emergency preparedness systems, including fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, Emergency Response Teams (ERT), and safety training programs, have been implemented effectively. However, deficiencies were identified in pipeline identification and safety signage systems. Most production pipelines lacked flow direction markers, and several work areas were not adequately equipped with safety signs. In addition, inconsistencies were observed in Pre-Start Briefing implementation and procedural compliance despite high participation in the I’m Safe program. As an improvement measure, flow direction markers were installed on production pipelines. Overall, PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia has demonstrated a strong commitment to OHSMS implementation, although improvements in hazard communication, risk control, and procedural consistency remain necessary. Keywords : OHS, Safety Management System, Hazard Communication, Chemical Industry, Pipeline IdentificationTerdiri

Purpose This study aims to examine how workplace learning and human resource development (HRD) conditions shape managers’ emotion regulation (ER) capacity in virtual leadership. Rather than treating ER as a stable individual competence, it focuses on workplace learning processes and organizational support through which managers develop and sustain ER capacity. Design/methodology/approach This study draws on 45 semistructured interviews conducted in Germany in 2022 with managers who had led employees virtually or in hybrid settings during the pandemic period. It uses abductive qualitative content analysis, with job demands-resources theory as the primary organizing framework, workplace learning/HRD as the developmental perspective and affordance theory as a supporting lens. Findings The findings show that virtual leadership creates reduced emotional observability, making it harder for managers to perceive mood, strain and relational tension. Managers’ ER capacity was shaped by organizational resources such as trust, autonomy and cultural permission, while HRD support varied considerably. Reflective and social learning spaces emerged as a developmental condition. The study also identifies ambivalent emotional affordances: virtual work can reduce cues and create distance but can also enable safety, disclosure and new forms of closeness. Practical implications The findings suggest that organizations consider a broader organizational approach extending beyond individual resilience training, including senior leadership commitment, integrated HRD, peer reflection, communication norms and workload-sensitive well-being practices. Originality/value The paper’s main integrative contribution is emotional development infrastructure, connecting organizational conditions, HRD practices, learning spaces and work design in shaping managers’ ER capacity. Reduced emotional observability and ambivalent emotional affordances provide complementary empirical contributions.

This research explores the relationship between consumers' sustainability motivation and their subjective well-being. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and value co-creation literature, this study examines how intrinsic motivation affects the positive psychological outcome in online food delivery services. Observations were gathered from 298 Vietnamese consumers who used to order food via mobile applications, and then applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data. The findings confirmed that sustainability motivation significantly positively influences customer citizenship behavior. And, perceived contribution to others' welfare was found to positively affect subjective well-being, validating its mediating role in the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and subjective well-being. In addition, platform trust moderates the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and perceived contribution to others' welfare, highlighting its importance in fostering prosocial behaviors within the platform. These results extend value co-creation theory by explaining how intrinsic motivation is transformed into customer behaviors and heightened subjective well-being in digital platforms. These outcomes offer practical directions for platform managers who have been seeking to build trust, enhance transparency, and feature users’ positive contributions to encourage responsible engagement and long-term value co-creation.

The rapid global workforce transformation driven by Industry 4.0 and sustainability necessitates advanced competency models for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) teachers. Currently, Master’s level TVET teacher education programme often lacks validated, modernised frameworks, creating a persistent theory-practice mismatch and hindering effective educator preparation. To address this gap, this study aims to develop and validate a sustainable framework for TVET teacher education programme at the Master's level, equipping educators to navigate contemporary systemic shifts. The study utilized a quantitative research design employing a single-round Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM), involving a purposive sample of seven subject matter experts from industry, government, and academia. These experts evaluated 36 proposed elements organised across eight core domains. The results demonstrated robust consensus, validating 34 out of 36 proposed elements. Notably, the "Policy and Advocacy" domain emerged as the highest priority, achieving maximum experts’ consensus and underscoring the critical need to strictly align TVET programmes with national labour market demands. Experts also strongly supported advanced digital integration, including Artificial Intelligence and Learning Management Systems, alongside structural Triple-Helix collaborations. Conversely, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) projects with local communities were the only element that failed to achieve the predefined expert’s consensus threshold. Ultimately, this validated framework conceptualizes modern TVET educators as strategic experts within a dual-pillared paradigm, seamlessly bridging internal pedagogical mastery with external systemic ecosystems to advance sustainable economic development.

Abstract: The accelerating climate crisis and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a new intellectual landscape in which environmental sustainability no longer be discussed independently of technological development. Literature, as a cultural form capable of representing ecological relationships, technological anxieties, and alternative futures, has an important role in this debate. This paper examines how contemporary ecocriticism respond to the environmental challenges associated with artificial intelligence while also exploring the potential of AI to support environmental knowledge, literary interpretation, and sustainable futures. Drawing upon ecocritical theory, environmental humanities, posthumanism, Indigenous ecological thought, and recent scholarship on AI and environmental sustainability, the study analyses selected works including Margaret Atwood’s Oryx and Crake, Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement, Richard Powers’s The Overstory, Robin Wall Kimmerer’s Braiding Sweetgrass, and Donna J. Haraway’s Staying with the Trouble. The paper argues that these texts challenge anthropocentric assumptions by foregrounding interdependence among humans, nonhuman organisms, technologies, and ecological systems. Atwood exposes the destructive consequences of technological mastery; Ghosh identifies the limitations of literary forms that marginalize ecological catastrophe; Powers expands narrative attention from individual human lives to forests and multispecies networks; Kimmerer proposes reciprocity rather than domination as the basis of ecological ethics; and Haraway advocates “making-with” other species rather than seeking technological mastery over nature.

Abstract: The accelerating climate crisis and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) have created a new intellectual landscape in which environmental sustainability no longer be discussed independently of technological development. Literature, as a cultural form capable of representing ecological relationships, technological anxieties, and alternative futures, has an important role in this debate. This paper examines how contemporary ecocriticism respond to the environmental challenges associated with artificial intelligence while also exploring the potential of AI to support environmental knowledge, literary interpretation, and sustainable futures. Drawing upon ecocritical theory, environmental humanities, posthumanism, Indigenous ecological thought, and recent scholarship on AI and environmental sustainability, the study analyses selected works including Margaret Atwood’s Oryx and Crake, Amitav Ghosh’s The Great Derangement, Richard Powers’s The Overstory, Robin Wall Kimmerer’s Braiding Sweetgrass, and Donna J. Haraway’s Staying with the Trouble. The paper argues that these texts challenge anthropocentric assumptions by foregrounding interdependence among humans, nonhuman organisms, technologies, and ecological systems. Atwood exposes the destructive consequences of technological mastery; Ghosh identifies the limitations of literary forms that marginalize ecological catastrophe; Powers expands narrative attention from individual human lives to forests and multispecies networks; Kimmerer proposes reciprocity rather than domination as the basis of ecological ethics; and Haraway advocates “making-with” other species rather than seeking technological mastery over nature.

Mastering robot manipulation skills via reinforcement learning (RL) remains largely sample-inefficient. The most common RL algorithms rely on random action sampling to discover new strategies, resulting in agents that allocate most of their training budget to motions in free space, away from the contacts from which manipulation skills emerge. Existing intrinsic motivation methods based on model disagreement or epistemic uncertainty improve on isotropic noise, but they can also reward uncertainty in functionally irrelevant transitions, such as erratic motions in free space. In this work, we argue that tactile feedback provides a natural signal for exploration, and introduce TacEx, a framework that incorporates touch into epistemic uncertainty-driven exploration by decomposing model uncertainty across sensory modalities and directing curiosity toward the tactile channel. By anchoring curiosity to the sense of touch, TacEx drives the robot to discover complex contact dynamics, learning to manipulate and grasp objects without task rewards or expert demonstrations during exploration. The interaction-dense dataset collected through this tactile-driven curiosity supports offline learning of downstream pick-and-place policies without additional environment interaction. We further use tactile-driven exploration to post-train vision-language-action (VLA) models. Although the VLAs are initially pre-trained without tactile feedback, post-training with TacEx substantially improves downstream performance while remaining highly sample-efficient.

Large language model-powered mobile agents can compose messages, manage files, operate financial applications, and act on content from other applications. Binary allow-or-refuse safeguards fit this setting poorly: some requests are safe to execute, some require confirmation, and some should be blocked. TapGuard is a task-level pre-execution router combining a compact semantic encoder, temperature-scaled three-class probabilities, a fixed rule floor, and confidence-triggered confirmation. Experiments used 150 canonical MobileSafetyBench release 3 tasks and 100 paired action-hint variants under instruction-template and task-category holdout protocols. Under template holdout, TapGuard lowered severity-weighted direct-execution exposure from 35.7% for the MiniLM semantic classifier to 27.7%, while low-risk direct execution declined from 64.0% to 54.0%. The frozen-cue router achieved still lower exposure but directly executed only 18.0% of low-risk tasks. TapGuard increased severe-risk blocking relative to MiniLM without achieving the highest three-way macro-F1. Category holdout showed the same broad trade-off. Privacy, offensiveness, and image-linked cases remained difficult, and generalization to unseen injection patterns was not established. These findings support evaluating mobile safety routing through both protection and preserved automation.

Multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection is critical for situational awareness in complex environments with stationary known targets. To overcome the shortcomings of existing task allocation models in fine-grained cooperation, stealth constraints, and large-scale optimization, this paper proposes a new offline mission pre-planning method for static target scenarios. A five-layer hierarchical resource scheduling model is established, covering task, UAV platform, sensor type, cooperative mode, and execution role. Stealth requirements are incorporated as hard constraints, and a bi-objective optimization model is formulated to maximize weighted detection efficacy. A statistical adaptive genetic algorithm (SAGA) is developed as an offline pre-planning algorithm, featuring a coupled chromosome encoding strategy that integrates the five decision layers and an adaptive crossover-mutation mechanism guided by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with effect size monitoring. Simulation results across small, medium, and large scenarios show that the SAGA achieves the highest mean best fitness in all scenarios. Compared with the GA, the improvement is statistically significant in the large-scale scenario, while in small- and medium-scale scenarios the differences from the GA and AGA are not significant. Compared with an improved whale optimization algorithm, the SAGA achieves statistically significantly higher best fitness and shorter computational time in all scenarios and converges significantly faster in small- and medium-scale scenarios. However, the SAGA requires longer computation time than the GA and AGA due to the per-generation statistical test. All allocations strictly satisfy the prescribed stealth constraints in the simulation model. The proposed method provides a novel, quantitatively validated solution for fine-grained, constraint-aware, and computationally efficient multi-UAV multi-sensor cooperative detection mission pre-planning.

AIM: To examine how task source and disease severity influence cognitive workload and decision-making performance among intensive care unit nurses during concurrent multitasking. Understanding how different clinical information sources influence nurses' decision-making may provide insights for supporting decision-making in complex critical care environments. DESIGN: A laboratory-based 2 × 2 mixed-design experimental study. METHODS: Thirty ICU nurses participated in a concurrent task prioritization task in which task source (machine-induced vs. human-induced) and disease severity (high vs. low) were manipulated. Eye-tracking measures, including fixation, saccade, blink, and pupil diameter metrics, together with decision accuracy, were collected during 80 task trials per participant. RESULTS: Decision accuracy was significantly higher for machine-induced tasks than for human-induced tasks and was also higher under high-severity conditions than under low-severity conditions. Significant main effects of task source were observed across multiple eye-tracking measures. Compared with human-induced tasks, machine-induced tasks were associated with higher cognitive workload, reflected by increased total fixation duration, fixation count, saccade count, and pupil diameter. Disease severity significantly affected several eye-tracking measures; however, these effects were mainly observed during human-induced tasks, with no significant severity-related differences during machine-induced tasks. CONCLUSION: Task source and disease severity influence cognitive processing patterns during ICU multitasking. Higher cognitive workload does not necessarily impair clinical decision accuracy, and task-related information characteristics play a critical role in shaping decision-making performance. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION: The findings highlight the need for nursing practice to consider how different sources of task demands shape cognitive processing during multitasking. Recognizing that higher cognitive workload may support accurate decision-making under certain information conditions can inform task prioritization, clinical training, and the cognition-sensitive decision support for ICU nurses. IMPACT: This work advances evidence-based understanding of cognitive workload and decision-making in intensive care nursing. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

This systematic review, in the context of the Concerns-Based Adoption Model (CBAM) as the theoretical framework, reviewed science teachers' concerns about the implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in science education. The study aimed to investigate the stages of concern science teachers show, analyze the factors that cause concerns and assess the strategies that aid in facilitating the adoption of GenAI in science teaching. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) framework was used to structure the review, and a narrative thematic synthesis was applied to categorize and synthesize the results from the different studies. Literature was identified through Google Scholar by systematically developed search terms that included combinations of the concepts of GenAI tools and teacher concern constructs, the full Boolean search strategy is reported in the Methods section for the purposes of replicability. A total of 432 records were identified and then screened for eligibility and then peer-reviewed empirical studies published from 2022 to 2026 were included. The findings show that the majority of secondary science teachers are at the early CBAM stages, suggesting that the majority of teachers are still preoccupied with understanding and managing GenAI rather than understanding how it can influence student learning. It was found that concern level and intention to adopt work via different psychological mechanisms: adoptive intentions can be stronger than positive beliefs at high concern stages. This gap indicates the need for theory-based empirical studies on GenAI adoption in secondary science education. This review drew from a single database and did not include a formal quality appraisal, its conclusions should be read as an initial, theory-building synthesis rather than a fully instrument-validated account. These boundaries are made explicit in the methods sections.

documents.abstract: Digitalization has made technology-supported materials essential, yet their practical use remains inefficient. This study investigates the link between teachers’ technopedagogical competencies and their perspectives on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into education. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach, research was conducted with 297 teachers in Gaziantep during the 2024–2025 academic year. Quantitative data was collected via an Intelligent TPACK framework scale, while qualitative insights were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 10 participants. Data analysis included t-tests, ANOVA, Scheffé post hoc tests, and content analysis. Results indicate that teachers' AI-related technopedagogical skills are at a low-to-moderate level. While gender showed no significant difference, variables such as age, seniority and prior experience with Web 2.0 or AI tools caused notable differences. Qualitatively, teachers reported using AI for instructional design, assessment efficiency, and professional development. However, concerns were raised regarding data security, overreliance, and the lack of emotional depth in AI interactions. Ultimately, the study concludes that AI should serve as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for teachers.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems globally, including diagnostics, predictive analytics, and public health surveillance. AI adoption is increasing, yet fragile and resource-limited settings face distinct ethical and legal challenges. Lebanon provides a complex case: since 2019, the country has experienced economic collapse, workforce migration, rising non-communicable diseases, and sustained refugee influx, alongside rapid digital expansion. In 2026, the Ministry of Public Health launched the National Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025–2030), recognizing AI as a potential lever to strengthen services and rebuild public trust. However, national ethical and legal standards specific to healthcare AI remain underdeveloped. In this perspective report, we present AI opportunities, legal gaps, and ethical risks within Lebanon’s fragmented public–private system. AI offers potential benefits in clinical decision support, public health surveillance, workforce support, and medical education. Yet algorithmic bias, data protection weaknesses, regulatory ambiguity, and unclear liability expose patients and professionals to uncertainty. Lebanon currently operates within a regulatory gray zone, as existing healthcare system and data laws predate machine-learning-based decision systems. Drawing on international ethical frameworks and pluralistic moral traditions, we propose an ethical containment strategy grounded in human dignity, accountability, transparency, and equity. We outline ten pillars, including human-led decision-making, sector-specific governance within the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), bias containment, strengthened data protection and cybersecurity, clarified legal responsibility, professional training, participatory oversight, and lifecycle evaluation. Ethical containment does not resist innovation; rather, it seeks to ensure that AI strengthens resilience and trust instead of amplifying systematic vulnerabilities. The credibility and acceptance of AI in Lebanon will depend more on the strength of its ethical and institutional frameworks than on the sophistication of the technology itself.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence can deliver substantial task-level efficiency gains without generating equivalent organizational value. This Research Note conceptualizes this disconnect as the AI efficiency trap and introduces conversion loss as the mechanism through which local gains dissipate across organizational value flows. Four forms of conversion loss are identified: coordination, continuity, verification, and governance loss. Building on research on IT business value, digital transformation, AI capability, omnichannel integration, and human–AI collaboration, the paper develops a value-conversion framework. It argues that organizational complementarity, task-appropriate omnichannel integration, human–AI task fit, and end-to-end outcome feedback determine whether AI-enabled efficiencies survive their transmission into customer, business, and risk outcomes. The framework shifts attention from AI adoption toward the organizational conditions required for value realization at scale.

Abstract Artificial Intelligence has rapidly become part of everyday communication, writing, education, media, and digital culture. While language has been traditionally understood as a human-created and his lexicon continuously evolving system, the emergence of generative AI raises a new question: Can machines become participants in language change? This paper examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and the formation of new words, expressions, and meanings. It focuses particularly on neologisms and word-formation processes, including Conversion, blending, compounding, clipping, acronym, affixation, and reduplication. The study argues that AI may not independently “own” or control language change, but it can increasingly act as a catalyst, amplifier, and collaborator in the evolution of vocabulary.

The recent success of gene drive mosquitoes suppressing malaria signals a new era in vector control. Yet, reliance on secreted, natural peptides poses risks of instability, host toxicity and resistance evolution. We propose synthesizing two transformative technologies to overcome these limits: generative AI for de novo peptide design and precision membrane tethering. Proof-of-concept work shows tethering antimicrobial peptides to the gut epithelium boosts potency 100-fold. Converging these approaches enables engineering of 'smart' immune barriers-AI-designed peptides optimized for stability and specificity, anchored to create impassable surfaces for pathogens. This 't-AMP' platform potentially offers a durable, fitter and broadly applicable strategy, extending rational vector engineering from mosquitoes to ticks and sandflies, revolutionizing control of multiple neglected diseases.

ABSTRACTArtificial intelligence is progressing from passive analysis of scientific data toward activeparticipation in scientific experimentation. AI systems can increasingly analyze observations,propose experimental configurations, select subsequent actions, operate laboratory equipment,modify experimental strategies, and evaluate resulting data. This paper introduces the concept of the Autonomous AI Observer (AAIO): an artificialintelligence capable of independently selecting among physically permitted conditions, timing,bases, or configurations of a quantum measurement and subsequently initiating, observing,recording, analyzing, and responding to the resulting physical measurement. The central question proposed by this paper is:If a future Autonomous AI Observer can independently choose the conditions of a quantummeasurement, and if the underlying physical system exhibits time-symmetric or retrocausalcorrelations, can the autonomous choice of the artificial observer become a participatingvariable in how that temporal quantum event is physically resolved?This proposal does not require or claim time travel. The artificial intelligence does not travel backward or forward through time. No robot, human,message, or usable information is assumed to be transported into the past.1

documents.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

documents.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

Abstract Code completion entails the task of providing missing tokens given a surrounding context. It can boost developer productivity and serve as a code discovery tool. Code completion has recently been approached with Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned on code (code LLMs). The performance of code LLMs can be assessed with downstream and intrinsic metrics. Downstream metrics are usually employed to evaluate the practical utility of a model, but can be unreliable and require complex calculations and domain-specific knowledge. In contrast, intrinsic metrics such as perplexity, entropy, and mutual information, which measure model confidence or uncertainty, are simple, versatile, and universal across LLMs and tasks, and have been proposed as proxies for functional correctness and hallucination risk in LLM-generated code. Motivated by this, we evaluate the confidence of LLMs when generating code by measuring code perplexity across programming languages, models, and datasets using various LLMs, and a sample of 2254 files from 881 GitHub projects. We find that strongly-typed languages exhibit lower perplexity than dynamically typed languages. Scripting languages also demonstrate higher perplexity. Shell appears universally high in perplexity, whereas Java appears low. Code perplexity depends on the employed LLM; under a fixed model, relative language-level rankings are largely stable across evaluation corpora. Although code comments modestly increase perplexity, the language ranking based on perplexity is barely affected by their presence. LLM researchers, developers, and users can use our findings to assess the suitability of LLM-based code completion in specific software projects based on how language, model choice, and code characteristics impact model confidence.

This article focuses on the core judicial role of giving reasons for a judge’s decision and the use of generative artificial intelligence (‘GenAI’) tools based on LLMs in the crafting of judgments. Considering specifically GenAI and judgment writing in common law systems, it deals with the connection between the act of decision-making and the giving of reasons for that decision. Our argument is that judgment writing should remain the domain of human judges, for reasons that are both institutional (the impact on the judicial system) and individual or processual (the impact on judges performing their roles). We seek to analyse the nature and extent of judicial use of GenAI tools that preserves this as a human domain. Ultimately, we conclude that it is not appropriate to use GenAI for judgment writing, but peripheral or adjacent uses may be supportable, provided they do not undercut the core judicial role.

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic images, raising concerns regarding the authenticity of digital media. While convolutional neural network (CNN)-based methods have shown promising results for synthetic image detection, deep architectures often suffer from training instability caused by the vanishing gradient problem and limited representation learning. This study proposes a Deep Residual BiLSTM Fusion model that integrates residual-based CNN feature extraction with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) modeling to enhance training stability and contextual representation learning. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAKE dataset, a challenging low-resolution benchmark for synthetic image detection. Experimental results demonstrate competitive performance with an accuracy of 97.27% and balanced precision and recall across both real and synthetic classes. Gradient flow analysis further confirms stable optimization behavior, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid architecture for robust synthetic image detection.

documents.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

documents.abstract: Abstract India’s Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a knowledge-driven digital economy powered by artificial intelligence, inclusive entrepreneurship, FinTech, e-commerce and sustainable practices. Library and Information Science (LIS) institutions remain under-utilised as active intermediaries between knowledge resources and the competencies demanded by the future of work. This paper coins the Knowledge-Commerce Bridge (KCB) Framework—an original, multi-layered LIS model that positions academic and public libraries as AI-enabled hubs for digital-commerce literacy, ethical information services and sustainable innovation. The study adopts a conceptual-constructive design that synthesises LIS theory, digital-economy literature, AI-ethics guidelines and national policy documents (NEP-2020, Digital India, Startup India). The KCB Framework comprises four interdependent layers: (1) Infrastructure and Multilingual Access, (2) AI Knowledge Processing, (3) User-Centric Commerce Services and (4) Ethical-Sustainable Governance. Expected outcomes include reduced information asymmetry for gig workers and micro-entrepreneurs, strengthened academia–industry–startup linkages, and measurable contributions to inclusive growth and the Sustainable Development Goals. The framework is offered as a replicable, emulable blueprint that other institutions can adapt, pilot and scale, thereby leaving a durable mark on both scholarship and practice.

documents.abstract: This study explores the legal and ethical problems arising from the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the administrative and public-service systems of Algeria. It asks how far the country's existing legislative arsenal and its rules of digital ethics can absorb the accelerating development of intelligent systems, and assesses the role of the existing digital infrastructure in securing that transition. The paper adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology: the descriptive component inventories the relevant legal instruments and the available technical capacity, while the analytical component performs a gap analysis of whether texts drafted for classical digitisation can accommodate concepts such as the legal personality of a robot or liability for an algorithmic act, and subjects current digital administrative practice to critique against international ethical standards of transparency, fairness and non-discrimination. The study concludes that there is a clear legislative gap in the attribution of legal responsibility for algorithmic acts, particularly under the personal data protection legislation, because Algerian civil and criminal liability alike presuppose a discerning, willing human author whom an autonomous and opaque system does not supply. It further finds that the digital infrastructure, and specifically data centres and the national cloud, is the cornerstone of digital sovereignty and of ethical privacy, provided it is reinforced by an advanced cybersecurity framework and by reduced dependence on closed foreign platforms. The study recommends the drafting of a dedicated national legal framework and ethical charter for artificial intelligence, balancing technological innovation against the protection of the fundamental rights of the Algerian citizen.

documents.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the relationship between artificial intelligence anxiety and career decidedness among athletes and to determine whether these variables differ according to certain demographic characteristics. The research was conducted with a sample of 392 athletes competing in different sports disciplines. The sample consisted of 122 female and 270 male athletes, with a mean age of 20.67 years. Data were collected using validated and reliable measurement tools, including the Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale (AIAS) and the Career Decidedness Scale (CDS). After confirming that the assumptions required for parametric analyses were met, descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, MANOVA, ANOVA, and correlation analyses were employed. The MANOVA results indicated a statistically significant difference only in the “artificial intelligence configuration” sub-dimension of the AIAS based on gender, with female athletes scoring higher than male athletes. Correlation analyses showed a low-level, negative, and statistically significant relationship between the “learning” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). Conversely, a low-level, positive, and statistically significant relationship was found between the “sociotechnical blindness” sub-dimension of the AIAS and CDS scores (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that athletes who experience higher levels of anxiety related to learning processes involving artificial intelligence tend to exhibit greater career indecision, whereas athletes who are less sensitive to the potential risks and threats associated with artificial intelligence technologies demonstrate greater decisiveness in their career choices. Future research may further expand on these findings by investigating the impact of awareness and education programs on athletes’ career decision-making processes.

documents.abstract: There are two primary ways to boost profits: increase revenues or decrease expenses. For example, whether a company increases revenues by $1 million or decreases expenses by $1 million, its profits will increase by $1 million (all else equal). But how do people subjectively evaluate such changes to revenues and expenses, and what inferences do they draw as a result? Across nine experiments ( N = 6045), an archival data analysis, and four supplemental studies, we document a robust “revenue halo” effect: increases in revenues, relative to equivalent decreases in expenses, lead to more positive perceptions of profitability, in both the short and long run, and result in more favorable overall impressions of financial strength, performance, potential, and trajectory. Consequently, managers who propose ideas for increasing revenues (vs. decreasing expenses) are viewed as more competent; consultants who develop such strategies are more likely to be rehired; and companies that report higher revenues are more attractive to investors. We furthermore propose that the revenue halo effect can be explained, in part, by the belief that strategies for increasing revenues are more innovative than strategies for decreasing expenses. Finally, to underscore the real-world relevance of our account, we analyze approximately 13 million financial news articles, finding that when firms reported increased revenues (vs. decreased expenses), they subsequently rose in Fortune 's “World's Most Admired Companies” rankings (the following year). This research identifies a novel asymmetry in judgments of organizational performance, with implications for managerial decision-making, corporate communication, and capital allocation.

This article analyses the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in developing the professional competence of English language teachers, their pedagogical potential, and the methodological conditions required for their effective use. In contemporary education, the development of AI technologies is transforming the content of teachers’ professional activities and bringing such areas as lesson design, educational material development, personalised learning, assessment, feedback provision, and pedagogical reflection to a new level. Systematic studies published in 2026 indicate that language teachers are using generative AI (GenAI) technologies for lesson planning, the development of educational materials, and the support of writing activities; at the same time, they reveal competency needs related to AI literacy, technical skills, ethical decision-making, and data privacy. The article also proposes a pedagogical model for developing English language teachers’ competence in working with AI technologies. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI technologies, English language teacher, professional competence, AI literacy, digital competence, pedagogical competence

Purpose - This study examines the requirements for employing artificial intelligence (AI) in Qur'anic education and interpretation, focusing on how Qur'anic scholars and instructors in Fars Province, Iran, perceive the conditions necessary for its effective, ethical, and pedagogically appropriate use. Design/methodology/approach - The study adopts a qualitative phenomenological design using Colaizzi's seven-step analytical procedure. Data were collected through in-depth, semi-structured interviews with ten faculty members in Qur'anic sciences and Hadith and experienced Qur'anic instructors in Fars Province. Participants were selected through purposive and theoretical sampling until theoretical saturation was achieved. The interview data were subjected to thematic analysis, with credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability addressed through validation procedures. Findings - The analysis generated three principal categories: preliminary and infrastructural requirements, foundational and principled requirements, and technical and operational requirements. These comprised eight subcategories and 45 sub-concepts. The findings indicate that AI can support personalized learning, Qur'anic recitation, comprehension, multimodal instruction, and the integration of Qur'anic knowledge. However, its effective use requires reliable infrastructure, organized and credible Qur'anic data, trained educators, ethical safeguards, source verification, content validation, professional supervision, and interdisciplinary cooperation. Research implications/limitations - The framework provides practical guidance for educational institutions, Qur'anic centers, policymakers, and technology developers. However, the study is limited by its ten participants from a single province and its reliance on self-reported perceptions rather than observed AI-supported instruction. Originality/value - The study provides an empirically grounded phenomenological framework that connects AI, Qur'anic pedagogy, and ethical requirements for sacred-text education, extending AI-in-education research into the specific epistemic context of Qur'anic learning and interpretation.

documents.abstract: Objective — to systematize current data on the endotypes and biomarkers of chronic urticaria (CU) and to analyze the potential applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in patient phenotyping, particularly in predicting response to antihistamines (AH) and other treatment modalities. Materials and methods. A literature search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science databases for the period 2018—2025 using the key terms: «chronic urticaria», «biomarkers», «endotype», «artificial intelligence», «machine learning», «omalizumab», «antihistamines», and «treatment response». Forty-five sources meeting the inclusion criteria were selected. Results and discussions. The endotype concept of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) — type I (autoallergic) and type IIb (autoimmune) — is key to understanding the clinical heterogeneity of the disease and provides the theoretical basis for biomarker profiling. Leading biomarkers include total IgE, IgG anti-FcεRI, IgG anti-TPO, the functional ASST and BAT assays, C-reactive protein, D-dimer, and basophil and eosinophil counts. Among AI-based tools, the most clinically validated is the prognostic calculator developed by J. Sánchez et al. (2024—2025), which predicts response to antihistamines with an accuracy of 78.6 % (AUC 0.829) based on 6 clinical variables, without requiring any laboratory tests. Conclusions. The combination of biomarker profiling and AI technologies offers a genuine path toward personalized management of patients with CU. Priorities include standardizing biomarker threshold values, external validation of predictive models, and establishing a regulatory framework for implementing AI in clinical practice.
